//: Checked once a day around 14:00: once the place has 2+ households or has held a meeting, every 5 days or so a new settlement out there takes notice (up to 3).
u = avatar.  A new settlement takes notice: a keep, the eyeglasses or the woodlanders (in turn, from a random start), with a name, a leader, a direction and a first view of you.

then.set_string_var: a fortified keep under a lord
an office of the old government's survivors, all clipboards and ration cards
forest folk, who keep to the trees and trade fair

//: One afternoon a week (day 4 of 7, 15:00-17:00): every settlement's agreement does its weekly work, and one of them (in turn) sends an envoy, if you're home.
The day before the week's tribute (day 3 of 7, by day, once): if the stores can't cover it, you're told.

One settlement's week: what an agreement brings (the woodlanders' food and seed, the eyeglasses' medicine, the keep's bolts), tribute paid out of the stores (or the agreement breaks), and a hostile one starts arming (a raid in 1-3 nights).

u = avatar.  What one settlement's envoy says at the gate (pass 6: the envoy walks in first, PF_NB_envoy), by how things stand: a family-minded one may offer a match (pass 6); hostile ones send nobody (they're arming); a friendly one (40+) offers to stand together; a keep with no agreement demands tribute; the eyeglasses offer registration for medicine, the woodlanders (and a keep that wants trade) offer trade; anyone already agreed just pays a courtesy visit (+5).

then.set_string_var: a fortified keep under a lord
an office of the old government's survivors, all clipboards and ration cards
forest folk, who keep to the trees and trade fair
An envoy from <global_val:pf_cur_name> wants everyone here registered and counted.  In return: medicine, every week.  Agree?

else.set_string_var: An envoy from <global_val:pf_cur_name> offers to trade: what they have for what you have, every week.  Agree?

effect.set_string_var: <global_val:pf_cur_lead> of <global_val:pf_cur_name> proposes a pact: if either place is attacked, the other comes.  Agree?
<global_val:pf_cur_lead> of <global_val:pf_cur_name> sends word: the land is theirs, and so is a share of what grows on it.  Five stores a week.  (The stores hold <global_val:pf_nb_have>.)  Pay?

//: u = avatar.  Who answers an envoy: the council if there is one (pass 6), else the chief (or lord) if someone else holds the chair and is here, else you (a popup).

u = the chief (or a councillor).  Tribute: they pay if the stores can bear it, unless they're proud (loyal and mother-hen chiefs pay; others half the time).  Anything else: their temperament plus how things stand with that settlement.
Every 30 minutes between 01:00 and 04:00, once a night: a settlement whose raid is due hits the place (one raid a night).

u = avatar, current settlement.  A raid, decided by strength against defense: the wall (+2), the watch being up (+2), a third of the grown-ups, an ally (+1), against an eighth of their people plus luck.  Held: they're driven off.  Not held: they take up to 10 stores and, if you're home, someone is hurt (a resident who was out there, bleeding).  Either way they think less of you.

then.u_make_sound: gunfire and shouting at the wall
shouting, running feet and something breaking

//: The morning after a raid got through while you were home: where they came in, and what's gone.
u = avatar.  Home menu: The neighbors.

u = avatar, pf_st_i = the settlement.  Pass 6: the envoy is a real person.  They're spawned 22 tiles out in the settlement's direction and walk to your door (one envoy on the road at a time); if nowhere out there will hold them, the word just arrives, as before.  Hostile settlements send nobody.

else.set_string_var: I've come from <global_val:pf_nv_from>, with word from <global_val:pf_nv_lead>.  It's for your door, where everyone can hear it.

//: u = the envoy, just spawned: marked, named, and sent to the door.

Every minute while an envoy is out: walking in, they're kept on their way to the door, and say their piece when they get there (or after 90 minutes, from the gate); leaving, they're removed once out of your sight.  If you go away, the visit is over (the envoy disappears on their own within the day).
u = the envoy (reached by unique id, only while you're near home).

then.set_string_var: I've said what I came to say.  I'll carry your answer back to <global_val:pf_nv_from>.

//: u = avatar.  The envoy is at the door: what they came to say (PF_NB_offer), and the answer goes home with them.
An envoy died on the way in (u = the envoy): their people think less of the place (-15).

u = avatar, pf_cur_* = the settlement.  A match: the single grown-up here (romantic, unpartnered, 50 or under) who most wants one (romantics and the sociable and loyal; loners and the proud less so).  If they're willing, the ruler answers (the council, the chief, or you).  Yes: in two days someone comes to marry them.

math: _w = 1 + u_has_trait('PF_Q_ROMANTIC') * 2 + u_has_trait('PF_T_SOCIABLE') + u_has_trait('PF_Q_LOYAL') - u_has_trait('PF_T_LONER') * 2 - u_has_trait('PF_Q_PROUD') + rand(2)

else.set_string_var: <global_val:pf_cur_lead> of <global_val:pf_cur_name> offers a match: one of theirs, to marry <global_val:pf_nb_mc_name> and make a home here.  <global_val:pf_nb_mc_name> is willing.  Agree?

//: Every 30 minutes, 10:00-17:00, once the day has come and you're home: the one from the other place arrives.

u = avatar.  The day has come: if the one promised is still here and still free, someone from the other place walks in from their direction to marry them.  They live here from now on (a resident with a job, in their partner's house), engaged, so the wedding is at the next evening's fire.  The two places are family now: no more arming against each other, and it counts toward the place's draw.
u = the one promised: still unpartnered and still living here?
u = the one who came to marry: romantic, drawn to the one they're marrying, devoted (for now), and living here.

u = the one promised, npc = the one who came: sweethearts, partners and engaged at once (the wedding is at the next evening's fire), with a little courting behind them so the match holds; they share a house.
